articles.title: Sem avanço nas negociações, Brasil pede à OMC para julgar tarifaço imposto pelos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Representantes dos dois países se reuniram em 25 de setembro e, com isso, foi aberto prazo de 60 dias para consenso. Em documento, Brasil informou que não houve acordo.
articles.summary: Representantes dos dois países se reuniram em 25 de setembro e, com isso, foi aberto prazo de 60 dias para consenso. Em documento, Brasil informou que não houve acordo.
articles.body:
O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) formalizou na Organização Mundial do Comércio ( OMC ) um pedido para que a entidade julgue o tarifaço imposto pelos Estados Unidos contra produtos brasileiros vendidos no mercado americano .

Conforme o pedido, o objetivo do Brasil é que a decisão sobre julgar ou não o tarifaço seja tomada no próximo dia 24, quando haverá uma reunião do Órgão de Solução de Controvérsias.

O documento entrou no sistema da OMC nesta quarta-feira (18), mas é datado do último dia 13.

Em 25 de setembro, representantes dos dois países se reuniram na sede da OMC , em Genebra (Suíça), para discutir o processo aberto pelo Brasil que questiona as tarifas.

Na prática, a partir da primeira rodada de negociação, passou a valer o prazo para que os dois países chegassem a um consenso.

Ao final desse prazo, sem acordo, qualquer um dos dois países poderia pedir a abertura de um painel.

"Foram realizadas consultas em 25 de setembro de 2026 com o objetivo de alcançar uma solução mutuamente acordada. Infelizmente, essas consultas falharam em resolver a disputa“, afirma o documento enviado pelo Brasil.

"Nesse sentido, o Brasil apresenta o seguinte pedido de constituição de um painel", conclui o governo brasileiro.

O pedido de consultas foi apresentado em julho deste ano . No documento, o Brasil questionou os dois tarifaços:

de 25% : diante do entendimento da Casa Branca de práticas desleais do Brasil em relação a empresários americanos em áreas como PIX, desmatamento e propriedade intelectual;

de 12,5% : em razão do entendimento dos EUA de que dezenas de países, incluindo o Brasil, falharam ao coibir a importação de mercadorias produzidas onde há trabalho forçado.

No pedido à OMC, o Brasil afirma que, ao agir dessa maneira, os EUA tratam o país de maneira diferente dos demais parceiros comerciais e ferem compromissos firmados junto à entidade .

Na resposta ao pedido de consultas, enviada em 10 de agosto, os EUA aceitaram o pedido e se disseram “à disposição” para discutir o tema .

Segundo integrantes do governo brasileiro, ainda não há, contudo, indicativo de reversão do tarifaço a partir do processo na OMC.

No mesmo dia em que os EUA aceitaram o pedido de consultas, o governo da China pediu formalmente para participar do processo .

O governo norte-americano, contudo, respondeu afirmando ser contra a presença dos chineses nas conversas.

A decisão de acionar o órgão tem um peso mais simbólico e institucional do que prático . Ao levar o caso à OMC, o Brasil formaliza a contestação às tarifas americanas e reforça a defesa das regras multilaterais de comércio, mesmo diante das limitações atuais do órgão para fazer suas decisões serem cumpridas.

O processo também mantém aberta uma via formal de negociação com os Estados Unidos e registra a posição brasileira dentro do sistema internacional de comércio.

O mecanismo da OMC tem o objetivo de assegurar que os países cumpram os acordos comerciais e que medidas consideradas incompatíveis possam ser contestadas.

Desde 2019, o órgão de apelação do principal mecanismo de resolução de disputas da OMC está paralisado , por conta de Donald Trump , que, ainda no seu primeiro mandato, barrou a nomeação de novos juízes.

Sem acordo com Brasil, EUA impuseram tarifas de 25% contra alguns produtos — Foto: Joao Oliveira/Zoonar/picture alliance

Assim, as chances de se chegar a um entendimento sobre as tarifas por meio da OMC são quase nulas.

Ao longo do processo de negociação entre os dois países, integrantes do governo brasileiro avaliam que a motivação do tarifaço contra produtores brasileiros era política e não comercial.

Os negociadores brasileiros citam entre os pontos que levaram a essa conclusão, por exemplo:

os EUA alegarem que têm déficit comercial com o Brasil, quando, na verdade, a relação é superavitária para os americanos;

os EUA argumentarem que o Brasil não combate o desmatamento como deveria, uma vez que os dados dos últimos anos mostram queda no desmatamento ilegal;

os EUA afirmarem que o Brasil falha ao importar mercadoria onde há trabalho forçado enquanto a OIT reconhece o país como referência no combate ao trabalho forçado.

Segundo auxiliares de Lula que participaram de uma recente conversa telefônica entre o presidente brasileiro e Trump, o presidente americano deu sinais de que não tem conhecimento dos pormenores do tarifaço.

articles.title: PGR denuncia Flávio Bolsonaro por calúnia contra Lula  | G1
articles.standfirst: Em uma rede social, o senador associou o então presidente da Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro, ao do presidente brasileiro, e fez menções aos crimes de tráfico de drogas e de lavagem de dinheiro.
articles.summary: Em uma rede social, o senador associou o então presidente da Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro, ao do presidente brasileiro, e fez menções aos crimes de tráfico de drogas e de lavagem de dinheiro.
articles.body:
Presidente reeleito Lula e o candidato derrotado Flávio Bolsonaro — Foto: Paulo Pinto e Joédson Alves/Agencia Brasil

A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) denunciou o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) por calúnia contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) ao fazer uma postagem atribuindo crimes como os de tráfico de drogas e de lavagem de dinheiro ao presidente.

No X (antigo Twitter), em 3 de janeiro de 2026, Flávio associou imagens do então presidente da Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro, a do presidente brasileiro, acompanhadas de um texto.

“Lula será delatado. É o fim do Foro de São Paulo: tráfico internacional de drogas e armas, lavagem de dinheiro, suporte a terroristas e ditaduras, eleições fraudadas”, escreveu.

O senador passou a ser investigado pelo caso em abril.

Ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), a PGR afirmou que a publicação no ultrapassou direito de crítica política e teve a intenção de atingir a honra do presidente.

O caso, ainda de acordo com a PGR, não está protegido pela imunidade parlamentar devido à gravidade das condutas imputadas e o manifesto intuito de ofender a honra objetiva do presidente da República.

“Embora se garanta ao denunciado, como parlamentar, o mais extenso direito de critica, do qual não se exclui a utilização de expressões ofensivas, a declaração objeto desta denúncia se deu em perfil pessoal do denunciado em rede social, longe, portanto, dos recintos próprios do Parlamento. A par disso, a gravidade das condutas imputadas e o manifesto intuito de ofender a honra objetiva do Presidente da República afastam a garantida prevista no art. 53 da Constituição que, conforme já reconhecido pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal, não pode ser utilizada como um "escudo protetivo para a prática de atividades ilícitas", disse a PGR.

O ministro Alexandre de Moraes, relator do caso, deve determinar abrir prazo para que Flávio Bolsonaro apresente resposta à acusação. Depois, o caso deve ser analisado pela Primeira Turma do STF, que vai decidir se o torna réu.

A PGR também avaliou que Flávio pode negociar um Acordo de Não Persecução Penal (ANPP) para evitar responder a um processo. No ANPP, o denunciado precisa admitir o crime e cumprir determinadas condições.

articles.title: Caso Master: Relatórios da PF sobre ministros causam tensão no STF | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministros temem que rito adotado por Fachin para análise do material provoque novos embates e desgastes da Corte. Gonet esteve com presidente do STF.
articles.summary: O caso Master atinge novo patamar com relatórios da PF citando seis ministros do STF, o que gera temor de novos desgastes institucionais e embates internos na Corte.
articles.body:
A confirmação da reunião entre o diretor-geral da Polícia Federal (PF), Andrei Rodrigues, e o presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), ministro Edson Fachin para a entrega dos relatórios da PF sobre ministros no caso Master provocou um clima de tensão no STF .

O encontro será na noite desta quarta-feira (18). Nos bastidores, há preocupação entre os ministros com as providências que serão adotadas pelo presidente da Corte após receber o material.

O receio é de que, a depender das medidas tomadas pelo presidente, o STF enfrente novos desgastes, embates públicos e vazamentos sobre as condutas de ministros.

Dos 10 ministros do Supremo, há citações, em graus diferentes, de pelo menos seis deles ou de seus parentes. A entrega dos relatórios deve pressionar ainda mais Fachin a atuar no caso.

O presidente do STF recebeu, no fim da manhã desta quarta, o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet . Depois, o ministro Alexandre de Moraes também esteve na Presidência.

Não há confirmação de que eles tenham tratado do material da PF.

Segundo interlocutores, o presidente do STF tem indicado que vai conversar com os colegas antes de definir os próximos passos. Fachin só deve decidir o destino dos relatórios após receber o material da PF.

A indicação é de que, num primeiro momento, o material não deve ser tornado público.

Uma das possibilidades é encaminhá-los para análise da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR).

O presidente do STF também pode avaliar a necessidade de uma análise interna preliminar, como ouvir a manifestação dos ministros citados.

Após ter acesso aos relatórios, outra questão que Fachin deverá decidir é se o material será compartilhado com os ministros e de que forma:

encaminhamento dos dados de todos os citados.

Edson Fachin e Andrei Rodrigues — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF e Divulgação

Ao receber, no início do ano, informações sobre as relações do ministro Dias Toffoli com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, Fachin compartilhou o documento com todos os colegas.

O episódio levou Toffoli a deixar a relatoria do caso Master, após surgirem informações sobre negócios que envolviam fundos do Banco Master na sociedade de um resort de sua família, no Paraná.

O ministro também passou a se declarar suspeito para analisar questões relacionadas à investigação na Segunda Turma.

articles.title: Câmara aprova projeto que pune político que não colaborar com transição entre governos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto tramitava desde 2007 e estabelece em lei o passo a passo para transição entre governos. Texto agora segue para análise do Senado.
articles.summary: A proposta aprovada pela Câmara estabelece regras para a transição entre governos e prevê multas para políticos que sonegarem dados ou dificultarem o acesso a informações.
articles.body:
A Câmara dos Deputados aprovou nesta quarta-feira (18) projeto de lei que regulamenta o processo de transição administrativa entre governos — o governo em exercício e um novo governo eleito. As regras valem tanto para o presidente da República, quanto governadores e prefeitos.

Pela proposta, o titular do cargo e o candidato proclamado vencedor deverão indicar uma equipe para a transição de governos em até 72 horas após a confirmação do resultado .

Caso haja resistência no processo de transição, o projeto prevê a aplicação de sanções administrativas e multa.

O projeto estava em tramitação na Câmara desde 2007 e agora segue para análise do Senado.

Nos casos de sonegação de informações ou de tentativa de impedir o novo governo eleito de acessar bancos de dados de informações, as punições serão agravadas e aumentadas em 1/3 das penas .

Também serão agravantes intimidar servidores ou agentes públicos que prejudiquem a transição.

A transição é um trabalho que exige a participação dos dois lados – o governo que está saindo e o governo que está chegando.

As regras para o processo de transição do cargo de Presidente da República estão listadas na Lei 10.609/2002 e no Decreto 7.221/2010. O decreto diz que a transição governamental começa com a proclamação do resultado da eleição e se encerra com a posse do novo presidente.

Plenário da Câmara dos Deputados durante sessão conjunta do Congresso Nacional destinada à deliberação de Projetos de Lei — Foto: Carolina Curi/Agência Senado

articles.title: Andrei entrega a Fachin relatórios sobre ministros no Caso Master | G1
articles.standfirst: Diretor-geral da PF disse que também entregou um HD com todas as mensagens citando ministros da Corte no caso Master. Relatório deve detalhar menções e citações aos ministros sem avançar sobre condutas criminosas.
articles.summary: PF entrega a Edson Fachin um HD com mensagens de Daniel Vorcaro citando seis ministros do STF, material que pode gerar novos desdobramentos no Caso Master.
articles.body:
O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, se reuniu na noite desta quarta-feira (18) com o presidente do Supremo Tribunal federal ( STF ), ministro Edson Fachin , para entregar o relatório citando todos os ministros do tribunal mencionados ou que trocaram mensagens com o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro.

O relatório deve detalhar menções e citações aos ministros sem avançar sobre condutas criminosas ou não . Os documentos chegam ao STF quando a primeira fase da Operação Compliance Zero, que investiga as fraudes do Master e suas conexões, completa um ano.

O diretor-geral chegou ao Supremo por volta das 19h20 para o encontro. A reunião durou cerca de uma hora.

Após encontro, Andrei afirmou que entregou todos os relatórios demandados pela Corte e um HD com a íntegra de todo o material.

"A Polícia Federal entregou todos os relatórios demandados aqui pela Corte. Além da entrega dos relatórios, entreguei também eh um HD com a íntegra de todo o material para que isso esteja também sob a custódia aqui da presidência do Supremo, bem como disponibilizei outros relatórios que foram produzidos em relação a esse episódio ao presidente Fachin também para que, se entender necessário, ele tem acesso. Então com isso, a Polícia Federal cumpre essa etapa, cumpre essa determinação da Suprema Corte que a partir de agora saberá certamente dar os encaminhamentos", disse o diretor-geral.

Nesta quarta, durante audiência pública no Senado, Andrei afirmou que vai enviar para Fachin um HD com todas as mensagens citando ministros da Corte no caso Master , além dos relatórios feitos pelos delegados e os novos, supervisionados por ele.

"Vou encaminhar o HD de todo material de onde saiu os relatórios e vou colocar à disposição do Fachin os relatórios dos delegados, que na minha avaliação não são adequados. Vou oficiar que está à disposição", disse Andrei.

Andrei Rodrigues, diretor-geral da PF, ao chegar no STF para reunião com presidente do Supremo, Edson Fachin — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Segundo ele, os relatórios dos delegados foram considerados inadequados não pelo conteúdo em si, mas pela forma como foram produzidos.

A confirmação da reunião entre o diretor-geral da PF e o presidente do STF provocou um clima de tensão no STF .

O receio é de que, a depender das medidas tomadas pelo presidente, o STF enfrente novos desgastes, embates públicos e vazamentos sobre as condutas de ministros.

Dos 10 ministros do Supremo, há citações, em graus diferentes, de pelo menos seis deles ou de seus parentes . A entrega dos relatórios deve pressionar ainda mais Fachin a atuar no caso.

Segundo interlocutores, o presidente do STF tem indicado que vai conversar com os colegas antes de definir os próximos passos. Fachin só deve decidir o destino dos relatórios após receber o material da PF.

A indicação é de que, num primeiro momento, o material não deve ser tornado público.

Segundo interlocutores, há pelo menos dois caminhos em análise por Fachin:

o envio para parecer da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR);

ou a análise interna, caso as questões sejam de âmbito disciplinar ou administrativo.

➡️ Se estiverem presentes elementos que indiquem infrações penais, os documentos devem ser encaminhados para avaliação da PGR.

Após ter acesso aos relatórios, outra questão que Fachin deverá decidir é se o material será compartilhado com os ministros e de que forma:

encaminhamento dos dados de todos os citados.

Presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin, e diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues — Foto: Reprodução

Ao receber, no início do ano, informações sobre as relações do ministro Dias Toffoli com o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, Fachin compartilhou o documento com todos os colegas.

articles.title: Only tore portion with Mani Shankar Aiyar’s face, says Shaina NC; Eknath Shinde backs her claim
articles.summary: Mumbai political row as Shiv Sena (UBT) accuses Shaina NC of disrespecting Bal Thackeray while tearing Sonia Gandhi’s memoir; Shaina, Shinde deny it.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A war of words broke out on Wednesday after Shiv Sena (UBT) accused Shiv Sena functionary Shaina N C of disrespecting the party’s late founder, Bal Thackeray, while tearing a page from Congress MP Sonia Gandhi’s memoir that had a photograph showing him hitting Congress veteran Mani Shankar Aiyar’s effigy with a slipper in 2004 for “insulting” Savarkar.While Sena (UBT) netas demanded a “public flogging” of those who insulted Thackeray, Shaina claimed that she had only torn the portion featuring Aiyar’s face. Sena chief and deputy CM Eknath Shinde backed her claim. “Balasaheb is our deity. He is like a god to us... Disrespecting or insulting him is completely out of the question. It will never happen,” he said.Sena claimed Sonia had insulted Savarkar in her book as well as the Marathi identity. It asked if Sena (UBT) chief chief Uddhav Thackeray, who had earlier sought a Bharat Ratna for Savarkar, would raise his voice against Sonia’s book.The controversy erupted during Sena’s protest against the memoir. Shaina and other party functionaries tore pages from the book on camera, along with photographs, including the one featuring Thackeray. The video went viral.Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut accused the rival faction of having “neither an ideology nor any morals”. “...All these people are mercenaries. It’s a good thing these black-faced people with white feet have run away. These people have... neither a single leader nor any loyalty. All these people who insult the honorable Balasaheb should be publicly flogged. I hope at least the Marathi people won’t object to my language,” he said.Shaina warned of legal action against those “spreading defamatory claims”. “Show me where I have torn or disrespected Hindu hruday samrat Balasaheb Thackeray’s photograph. Deliberately twisting an incident to create a false narrative will not be tolerated... I will tear Mani Shankar Aiyar’s photograph a thousand times over and this is what Balasaheb taught us,” she said.Shinde said his party is carrying forward Thackeray’s ideology. “Insulting him is impossible. Nobody can do that. Shaina N C has given a clarification... Balasaheb had taken to the streets to hit [Aiyar’s effigy] with a slipper. Where the photo was torn, it was Aiyar’s face. I saw that myself.”Congress slammed Shaina for targeting Sonia’s book. “The Shinde faction has reached the height of ideological bankruptcy. Tearing up a book cannot erase history, and distorting an image cannot diminish a person. By dishonoring the sacrifice of Indiraji, the martyrdom of Rajivji, and many other historical references, including those involving Balasaheb, what exactly are you trying to achieve politically? Has Shiv Sena, which has sold out and tied itself to BJP’s apron strings, become so desperate to preserve its own political existence? articles.title: Vadodara civic body allots land to Yusuf Pathan amid political storm
articles.summary: Vadodara Municipal Corporation approves 978 sq m land allotment in Tandalja to MP Yusuf Pathan amid Congress protests, with free and concessional transfer terms.
articles.body: VADODARA: Amid a major political storm, heated exchanges and protests, the BJP-ruled Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) on Wednesday approved by majority the proposal to allot a prime 978-sq-metre plot in Tandalja to former India cricketer and MP Yusuf Pathan, despite strong opposition from Congress councillors.The proposal, cleared unanimously by the standing committee on Oct 23, sparked an uproar in the general body, where BJP and Congress councillors traded barbs. The Congress accused the BJP-led state govt of changing its stand after Pathan extended support to the NDA.Confirming the approval, mayor Geeta Makwana said the proposal had come from the state govt. “There was some controversy because of the opposition, but since the proposal came from the state govt, we approved it by majority,” she told reporters after the meeting.On whether other cricketers seeking land would receive similar treatment, Makwana said, “If any proposal comes from the state govt, we will discuss it accordingly.” She maintained that the allotment was sanctioned according to the rules and regulations.The general body witnessed heated arguments after councillor Ashish Joshi questioned the BJP’s support for Pathan. “In my eyes, everyone supporting Yusuf Pathan is a Pathan,” he remarked, triggering an uproar. BJP councillor Ajay Dabhi retorted by calling him “Ashish Pathan”, prompting ruling party councillors to repeatedly raise slogans of “Ashish Pathan”.Joshi also asked why the BJP had rejected a proposal to pay Rs 25 lakh each to families of the 14 victims, including 12 children, who died in the Harni boat tragedy, while extending concessions on land worth over Rs 20 crore to Pathan. Congress councillors Pushpa Vaghela and Deepa Srivastava also strongly opposed the allotment.Outside the VMC headquarters, Congress workers attempting to enter the premises were stopped by police and security personnel, leading to a scuffle. Several Congress leaders, including the city Congress president, were detained and taken to Gotri police station, where party workers protested against the police action.Congress councillor Tirth Brahmbhatt arrived dressed in Pathani attire to oppose the decision. He questioned why similar consideration was not extended to Vadodara-born woman cricketer Radha Yadav, who had sought land for sports-related development. He also submitted representations seeking office space for councillors, residential plots for journalists and compensation for Harni boat tragedy victims.Senior Congress councillor Chandrakant Srivastava warned that the party would approach court if the proposal was approved.Under the approved proposal, 500 sq metres of the plot will be allotted to Pathan free of cost for residential use, while the remaining 478 sq metres will be transferred at 55% of its assessed value, offering a 45% concession. The plot’s estimated market value is Rs 20.53 crore. The state revenue department will compensate VMC with land of equivalent value for the portion allotted free.The controversy dates to 2012, when Pathan sought a 99-year lease of the plot adjoining his family residence. The state govt rejected the proposal in 2014, citing the need for public auction or open bidding. VMC subsequently alleged encroachment and issued Pathan a notice in 2024.Gujarat High Court upheld the rejection in Aug 2025, ruling that prolonged possession conferred no legal rights. Pathan unconditionally withdrew his appeal on Aug 31, 2026.The allotment also drew objections from Vishwamitri Bachao Samiti, which argued that it was contrary to the provisions and spirit of the Disturbed Areas Act. articles.title: Ajuste fiscal: Moretti diz que texto aprovado pelo Senado preserva políticas sociais essenciais em 2027  | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro do Planejamento se envolveu diretamente nas negociações da proposta.
articles.summary: Ministro do Planejamento se envolveu diretamente nas negociações da proposta.
articles.body:
Bruno Moretti, ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento — Foto: Edilson Rodrigues/Agência Senado

O ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti, disse nesta quarta-feira (18) que o pacote fiscal aprovado pelo Senado manteve a essência da proposta do governo de equilibrar as contas públicas e garantir recursos para manter políticas sociais essenciais no ano que vem.

“Nosso processo é de equilíbrio das contas, entregar o Orçamento no ano que vem, preservando nossas políticas públicas essenciais à população”, declarou.

A aprovação do pacote representou uma primeira vitória do governo depois da reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do ministro, que participou ativamente das negociações.

O texto precisa agora ser aprovado pela Câmara dos Deputados.

Atuação do ministro na articulação política

Na última quarta-feira (11), Moretti participou de uma audiência na Comissão Mista de Orçamento (CMO) , onde apresentou as linhas gerais da proposta e estimou um impacto de até R$ 60 bilhões nas contas públicas em 2027.

No dia seguinte, quando o texto-base foi aprovado pelo Senado, o ministro participou de conversas com parlamentares e lideranças do Congresso Nacional para explicar as medidas e buscar apoio.

Em meio à pressão do setor produtivo e de governadores, as negociações seguiram, com a atuação do ministro nos bastidores.

Na sexta-feira (13), Moretti se reuniu com o presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), para tratar da tramitação da proposta na Casa.

Na terça-feira (17), também conversou com a bancada do PT na Câmara, em meio à resistência de parlamentares governistas a pontos do pacote .

As tratativas em torno do texto avançaram até a votação final no Senado. Moretti acompanhou a articulação no plenário, enquanto os senadores aliados do governo buscavam evitar alterações expressivas no texto.

A votação dos destaques, inicialmente prevista para terça-feira, acabou adiada para esta quarta-feira (18), quando o pacote foi aprovado pelos senadores.

articles.title: PGR terá que analisar relatórios da PF sobre relação de Vorcaro com ministros do STF e apontar providências cabíveis; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Nesta quarta (18), presidente do STF se reuniu com o diretor-geral da PF e recebeu relatórios sobre a relação do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com os ministros da Corte.
articles.summary: Nesta quarta (18), presidente do STF se reuniu com o diretor-geral da PF e recebeu relatórios sobre a relação do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com os ministros da Corte.
articles.body:
A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) vai ter que apontar ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) quais as providências cabíveis em relação a cada relatório produzido pela Polícia Federal sobre a relação do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro com os ministros da Corte.

Nesta quarta-feira (18), a presidência do Supremo informou que vai encaminhar para análise da PGR os relatórios entregues pela PF.

A Procuradoria terá que dizer se considera que o conteúdo justifica a abertura de uma apuração, se é preciso aprofundar os fatos narrados com novas diligências, se há dados para medidas mais gravosas, como uma denúncia, ou se é o caso de arquivamento .

A análise, que deverá ser feita em 15 dias após o recebimento do material enviado pelo Supremo, pressiona o chefe do MPF, que enfrenta desgastes internos também pela crise do Master.

Nesta quarta, o procurador-geral da República, Paulo Gonet, esteve reunido com o presidente do Supremo, ministro Edson Fachin, antes da entrega dos relatórios pelo diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues .

Depois de receber as manifestações da PGR, caberá a Fachin avaliar se os casos devem ser submetidos plenário ou ainda se outras providências internas podem ser adotas, como pedido de manifestação dos ministros citados . Isso poderá arrastar os desdobramentos para 2027.

O entendimento da PGR não vincula automaticamente o plenário do STF , a quem cabe decidir, por exemplo, sobre a abertura de inquérito contra um integrante da Corte.

A análise dos documentos reunidos pela PF caberá a Paulo Gonet e à equipe dele que já atua no caso Master no STF, como o vice-procurador-geral da República, Hindenburgo Chateaubriand, e dois subprocuradores.

A análise pela PGR tem apoio de ministros das alas de Moraes e de Mendonça .

O encaminhamento dos casos para a Procuradoria, além de dar respaldo ao Supremo para decidir diante de uma análise técnica, ainda daria tempo para novas investidas para uma composição interna — apontada ainda como de difícil solução.

A PGR já chegou a se manifestar no Supremo pelo arquivamento de um relatório da PF sobre menções ao ministro Alexandre de Moraes, elaborado por determinação do ministro André Mendonça e que instalou uma crise institucional sem precedentes no Supremo.

A Procuradoria entendeu que havia vício na produção do relatório. O d ocumento apontou Moraes como interlocutor de 52 mensagens do banqueiro , que demonstravam apreensão com as investigações e pedidos de interferência.

Também foi apontada uma suposta análise e edição pelo ministro de um contrato de R$ 130 milhões, assinado entre o Banco Master e o escritório de advocacia Barci de Moraes, de Viviane Barci, esposa de Moraes.

A Procuradoria já havia se manifestado contra a apuração da conduta de Toffoli na relatoria do caso Master. A posição foi apresentada antes de um relatório da Polícia Federal indicar negócios entre fundos ligados ao Banco Master e uma empresa da família do ministro , envolvendo a sociedade de um resort no Paraná.

Isso levou o ministro a deixar a relatoria do caso Master e a se declarar suspeito para analisar questões da investigação.

Dos 10 ministros do Supremo, há citações, em graus diferentes, de pelo menos seis deles ou de seus parentes . Todos os ministros e familiares negam irregularidades ou envolvimento com Daniel Vorcaro.

articles.title: Marina JHC no Senado: entenda a disputa judicial sobre a candidatura | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatura foi deferida pelo TRE-AL, mas coligação adversária recorreu ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral alegando falta de desincompatibilização de cargo em fundação de ensino.
articles.summary: Candidatura foi deferida pelo TRE-AL, mas coligação adversária recorreu ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral alegando falta de desincompatibilização de cargo em fundação de ensino.
articles.body:
Um recurso que tramita no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) questiona a validade da candidatura de Marina JHC ( PSDB ), eleita senadora por Alagoas com 926.860 votos . O processo discute se ela cumpriu as exigências legais para disputar as eleições de 2026.

A candidatura foi aprovada pelo Tribunal Regional Eleitoral de Alagoas (TRE-AL) em 14 de setembro, mas, dois dias depois, em 16 de setembro, a coligação adversária Pra Alagoas Fazer História de Novo recorreu da decisão ao TSE.

O julgamento estava previsto para 12 de novembro, porém foi retirado de pauta e ainda não tem nova data. O relator é o ministro Dias Toffoli.

Em nota, Marina classificou o questionamento como uma “aventura jurídica” , destacou as manifestações favoráveis à sua candidatura e afirmou confiar na Justiça Eleitoral.

Ela não é a única pessoa eleita para o Senado que enfrenta questionamentos sobre sua elegibilidade. No Paraná, Deltan Dallagnol (Novo) também aguarda o julgamento de um recurso no TSE relacionado à Lei da Ficha Limpa.

Antes das eleições, a coligação Pra Alagoas Fazer História de Novo, que lançou Renan Filho ( MDB ) ao governo e Renan Calheiros (MDB) ao Senado, apresentou uma Ação de Impugnação ao Registro de Candidatura (AIRC) contra Marina.

O advogado eleitoral Marcelo Brabo explica que o processo envolve a desincompatibilização , obrigação de se afastar de determinados cargos ou funções antes de disputar uma eleição.

“A finalidade é preservar a igualdade entre os candidatos, evitando que as atribuições do cargo ou o acesso à estrutura pública proporcionem vantagem eleitoral”, afirma Brabo.

Marina não teria deixado dentro do prazo legal a função de conselheira da Fundação Educacional Jayme de Altavila (Fejal), mantenedora do Cesmac;

A fundação seria mantida pelo poder público, o que exigiria o afastamento definitivo da candidata;

Marina teria exercido funções de gestão em programas da Prefeitura de Maceió , mesmo sem ocupar oficialmente um cargo público.

Quais são os argumentos da coligação adversária?

Renan Filho e Renan Calheiros — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Marina tomou posse como conselheira da Assembleia Geral da Fejal em 30 de março e apresentou um pedido de afastamento temporário em 3 de julho. A coligação sustenta que ela deveria ter deixado a função até 4 de abril, seis meses antes das eleições.

A fundação mantém contratos com o Instituto Federal de Alagoas (Ifal) e firmou, em 2 de abril, um convênio com a Prefeitura de Maceió para a concessão de dez bolsas de estudo em Medicina.

A defesa argumenta que a Fejal é uma instituição privada , mantida principalmente pelas mensalidades dos estudantes, e que Marina não exercia funções executivas de gestão ou representação.

Sobre a atuação na prefeitura, a coligação alega que Marina continuou desempenhando atividades de coordenação de programas municipais mesmo após a renúncia do marido, JHC (PSDB), ao cargo de prefeito. A defesa sustenta que a condição de primeira-dama não configura função pública.

O g1 entrou em contato com a Fejal e com a Prefeitura de Maceió, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Marina Candia é anunciada por Flávio Bolsonaro como candidata ao Senado por Alagoas — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

A maioria dos desembargadores do TRE-AL entendeu que não ficou demonstrado que Marina exercia funções que exigissem seu afastamento da fundação. Com esse entendimento, o tribunal aprovou a candidatura ao Senado em 14 de setembro, por quatro votos a dois , rejeitando a ação da coligação adversária

O tribunal também considerou que a atuação como primeira-dama não configurava exercício de função pública e que as alegações de promoção pessoal e uso da máquina pública deveriam ser apuradas em outra ação eleitoral.

Em 22 de setembro, o vice-procurador-geral eleitoral, Alexandre Espinosa Bravo Barbosa, emitiu parecer favorável à manutenção da candidatura, concordando com o entendimento do TRE.

Apesar das manifestações favoráveis, Marcelo Brabo explica que o resultado do julgamento não pode ser antecipado.

“Tudo é uma questão interpretativa e de se saber se a situação se enquadra ou não dentre as causas de inelegibilidade”, afirma.

Quais são as chances de Marina manter a vaga?

Marina Candia ao lado do marido, o ex-prefeito de Maceió, João Henrique Caldas — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Para o advogado eleitoral Pedro Leal, a permanência de Marina no Senado é o cenário mais favorável neste momento.

“A manutenção do registro parece-me um cenário mais favorável por causa da decisão do TRE de Alagoas, do parecer favorável da Procuradoria-Geral Eleitoral e da exigência de prova efetiva de gestão no cargo”, avalia.

Leal destaca que a proximidade entre as datas da posse na fundação, da assinatura do convênio e do prazo de afastamento representa um ponto de atenção, mas que não ficou comprovado no processo que Marina praticava atos de gestão.

O TSE poderá manter ou negar o registro da candidatura. Outra possibilidade é determinar o retorno do processo ao TRE para a produção de novas provas, conforme solicitado pela coligação adversária.

Como a ação discute a elegibilidade de Marina, o pagamento de uma multa não substituiria o indeferimento do registro caso o tribunal reconhecesse um impedimento legal à candidatura.

Marina pode assumir o mandato antes da decisão?

Sim. Enquanto o registro da candidatura estiver válido, Marina poderá ser diplomada e tomar posse mesmo que o processo continue em andamento.

O prazo para a diplomação termina em 18 de dezembro. A posse dos novos senadores está prevista para 1º de fevereiro de 2027.

Segundo Pedro Leal, uma eventual decisão desfavorável após a diplomação poderá resultar na anulação do diploma ou na perda do mandato , caso Marina já tenha assumido o cargo.

Ainda cabem recursos ao próprio TSE e ao Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), mas eles não suspendem automaticamente os efeitos da decisão.

Caso a candidatura seja invalidada, Alagoas deverá realizar uma eleição suplementar. Nem os suplentes de Marina nem Renan Calheiros (MDB), terceiro colocado na disputa, assumiriam automaticamente a cadeira.

“Haveria a cassação da chapa, os votos dela seriam anulados, e aí se lançaria uma nova eleição. Não há uma mudança automática dentro desse pleito”, explica Pedro Leal.

A realização de uma nova eleição está prevista no artigo 224 do Código Eleitoral. Até a posse do vencedor, a cadeira permaneceria desocupada. A vaga conquistada por Arthur Lira ( PP ) não seria afetada pelo processo.

articles.title: Fim da escala 6x1: Lula assina decreto da jornada 5x2 nesta quinta | G1
articles.standfirst: Fim da escala 6x1 foi uma das promessas de campanha do petista. Um decreto do presidente definirá as regras, como para a transição que já deve ocorrer em dezembro.
articles.summary: O fim da escala 6x1 será regulamentado por decreto de Lula nesta quinta-feira, definindo a transição para a jornada 5x2 e redução de horas sem corte salarial.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) deve assinar nesta quinta-feira (19) o decreto que regulamenta o fim da escala 6x1. O texto vai definir as regras de transição do regime atual para a jornada 5x2.

Segundo o ministro, Lula teria pedido algumas alterações no texto, mas não quis detalhar quais.

O fim da escala 6x1 foi um das principais temas da campanha do presidente à reeleição.

De acordo com o texto da emenda que acabou com a escala 6x1, aprovada no Senado Federal em 14 de outubro, a transição para a escala 5x2 deve começar já em 16 de dezembro de 2026, com a redução da jornada 44 para 42 horas semanais.

Além disso, também começa a valer no próximo mês a obrigatoriedade de dois dias de descanso semanal.

A segunda etapa da transição prevê que, 12 meses depois da primeira redução, a carga horária máxima deve cair definitivamente para 40 horas semanais, sem redução salarial.

🔎 Foi a primeira mudança na jornada de trabalho em 38 anos, desde a Constituição de 1988.

O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), concedeu uma decisão liminar autorizando que a jornada intermediária de 42 horas semanais seja distribuída em cinco dias, na escala 5x2, com expedientes diários de até 8 horas e 24 minutos, sem a incidência de adicional de hora extra pelos 24 minutos.

Carteira de trabalho — Foto: Jorge Júnior/Rede Amazônica

A autorização vale especificamente para a etapa de transição prevista na emenda constitucional que alterou a jornada de trabalho.

No início deste mês, durante a coletiva do Caged, o ministro do Trabalho e Emprego explicou que as negociações sobre os dias de folga do trabalhador vão ser feitas por acordo de convenção coletiva negociado pelos sindicatos.

Cada setor vai precisar se enquadrar no melhor modelo que atenda àquela atividade econômica, mas respeitando obrigatoriamente as 8 folgas por mês sem redução de salário.

articles.title: Cornyn blocks Trump’s nomination to federal district court because he didn’t choose a Texan
articles.summary: Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) on Wednesday blocked President Trump’s judicial nominee T. Elliot Gaiser from being confirmed for a seat on the U.S. District Court in the Northern District of Texas because the nominee is not from Texas. Cornyn, the outgoing senator to be succeeded by Sen.-elect James Talarico (D-Texas), did not submit a blue…
articles.body:
Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) on Wednesday blocked President Trump’s judicial nominee T. Elliot Gaiser from being confirmed for a seat on the U.S. District Court in the Northern District of Texas because the nominee is not from Texas.

Cornyn, the outgoing senator to be succeeded by Sen.-elect James Talarico (D-Texas), did not submit a blue slip for Gaiser. This process is a Senate Judiciary Committee tradition where the chair asks home-state senators to assess the nominee. If withheld or returned with rejections, the process does not generally move forward.

A Cornyn aide told The Hill’s The Gavel that he instead pushed the White House for months to recommend Steve Fahey, a former federal prosecutor, for the vacancy. Cornyn accused the White House of having “completely ignored” his requests and said he was “not willing to let the White House ignore the Senate’s constitutional role.”

Gaiser was expected to appear before the Senate Judiciary Committee for a confirmation hearing on Wednesday but was not among the seven candidates for federal judgeships to testify.

“I just refuse to be jammed by a non-Texan who has no trial experience, who hasn’t been vetted,” Cornyn told CNN . “And so, we provided the White House an alternative, and I’m hoping they take advantage of it because I don’t want the seat to go vacant either.”

Cornyn told CBS News that Gaiser’s nomination was “no longer viable.”

“He’s not a Texan, has no trial experience, and the White House tried to jam the Senate and wouldn’t allow us to do our due diligence that we need to do on lifetime appointments,” he told the outlet.

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

Gaiser lived in Ohio before he was tapped to lead the Office of Legal Counsel at the Department of Justice. Trump formally sent Gaiser’s nomination on Monday.

Gaiser issued a classified legal opinion justifying lethal strikes against drug cartels and suspected drug traffickers, CNN reported last month. He said that the strikes did not trigger the war powers law due to not meeting the definition of “hostilities,” the network added.

The Ohioan also ruled in August that Trump’s outside advisers are protected from any future congressional and legal investigations, with internal communications with these outside advisers protected by executive privilege.

Other lame-duck Republican lawmakers have indicated that other judicial nominees could face roadblocks to their confirmation, including Trump’s choice for the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Oklahoma, attorney Zach West. Sen. Alan Armstrong (R-Okla.) withdrew his support for West, while Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) said he may not drop his opposition.

“Frankly, it’s an unforced error by the White House just not to consult more effectively with Senator Armstrong,” Tillis told Bloomberg . “I think he’ll get done, but they’re running it down to the wire.”

articles.title: BAAJA passes another procedural vote
articles.summary: Presented by EQT {beacon} Energy & Environment Energy & Environment The Big Story BAAJA passes another procedural vote The Senate took a series of key votes on Wednesday to advance a permitting reform bill that seeks to speed up the nation’s ability to build infrastructure and energy. © Greg Nash The upper chamber advanced the…
articles.body:
The Senate took a series of key votes on Wednesday to advance a permitting reform bill that seeks to speed up the nation’s ability to build infrastructure and energy.

The upper chamber advanced the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) 65-31 in a procedural vote known as a cloture vote, helping it move toward final passage and overcoming the Senate’s 60-vote threshold.

This is not a surprise, as the legislation has also advanced in other recent votes, though it represents the formal clearance of a key hurdle to the bill becoming law.

While there were enough votes to pass, it appears some support has been dropping off. A vote early last week, for example, passed 73-25 .

Sens. Josh Hawley (Mo.) and Mike Rounds (S.D.) were the only Republicans to vote against the legislation Wednesday. Rounds had previously voted against the bill, citing disagreement with some of the bill’s provisions on power lines . Hawley previously voted to advance debate on the bill, but he opposed the bill in a procedural vote earlier this week.

The measure is still expected to go through an amendment process as some lawmakers have insisted on tweaks, including addressing concerns from tribes that its changes to historic preservation law don’t give them adequate input into projects that may impact them. It’s not clear whether these or any other amendments will make it into the bill’s final text.

articles.title: Musk on midterms spending: ‘I feel pretty foolish’
articles.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday said he feels “pretty foolish” after he spent $442 million toward Republican campaigns in the 2026 midterm elections, where the party saw sweeping losses to Democrats. Musk, the world’s richest person, told New York Times columnist Andrew Ross Sorkin virtually at the DealBook Summit that his goal was to have…
articles.body:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday said he feels “pretty foolish” after he spent $442 million toward Republican campaigns in the 2026 midterm elections, where the party saw sweeping losses to Democrats.

Musk, the world’s richest person, told New York Times columnist Andrew Ross Sorkin virtually at the DealBook Summit that his goal was to have Republicans keep control of the Senate. Democrats won a majority and claimed another victory after Democrat Mary Peltola won her Senate race in Alaska, giving the party 56 seats to the GOP’s 44.

“I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” Musk told Sorkin. “Or maybe it would’ve been much worse without that. But it certainly shows that American elections are not just about money. Obviously you can put a lot of money into an election and have an effect that is relatively minor, and I think that was the case here.”

“So probably if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money, and I didn’t put a lot of personal attention into it because I’m focused on building SpaceX, Tesla,” he added.

He later said that his motivation was to have the House, Senate or the White House be controlled by Republicans going into 2029, though he said he did not want either a “supermajority” of Democrats or Republicans.

“I think we have some want to have some checks and balances here,” Musk said. “And that was it, really. So, you know, I think I’m ideologically quite moderate. I don’t think I like, you know, any kind of extreme political views.”

Musk said in the interview that he’s “not MAGA” and that he was not sure what it means, “but if that means, sort of, blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.”

This stark admission follows Musk’s previous close relationship with President Trump in the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election and subsequent hiring as the head of the now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).

How the two operated prompted some critics to claim they ran a “co-presidency,” though the two feuded before Musk eventually left his role to focus on his companies and DOGE shut down in July after its executive order mandate expired.

In October 2024, Musk said he was “dark gothic MAGA” during a Trump rally at Madison Square Garden, wearing a black MAGA hat with a font criticized as resembling the font Fraktur, which the Nazis used during their reign in Germany. Experts have since debunked this .

Musk has championed other right-wing political parties globally. He notably appeared virtually at a rally in January 2025 for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. The party’s landslide victory in the German state Saxony-Anhalt last month was described by Georgetown University researchers as opening “the possibility of Germany’s first far-right state government since the Nazi era.”

articles.title: Sen. Elissa Slotkin fires back at DOJ official over investigation of her political speech
articles.summary: U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz has suggested that Slotkin’s comments about congressional oversight could amount to a criminal civil rights offense.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — A Democratic senator repeatedly targeted by the Trump administration for potential prosecution due to her political remarks is firing back at a Trump-appointed Justice Department official over what she called a “baseless” inquiry into her rhetoric about congressional oversight. Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., is one of five Democratic members of Congress who have been the subject of letters that U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas Aaron Reitz has posted on social media. In one of the letters, which have come under scrutiny from legal experts, Reitz suggested that Slotkin’s comments about congressional oversight potentially acting as a “deterrence message” to people considering joining the Trump administration could amount to a criminal civil rights offense. “I made those statements consistent with my basic right to freedom of speech, a right that every American enjoys under the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution,” Slotkin wrote Wednesday in a letter to Reitz obtained by NBC News. “In addition to my First Amendment rights, as a United States Senator, oversight is an important constitutional responsibility.” “The Constitution’s Speech or Debate clause bars prosecution of a legislator for conducting an investigation or performing other legislative acts,” she wrote. “As such, your threat of investigation is baseless, and you should withdraw your letter immediately.” Slotkin went on to say that Reitz’s “public threats” violated Justice Department policy, and that his decision to publicly post the letter rather than providing it to her, her attorney, or Senate legal counsel “is evidence that your threat of investigation is more about publicity and your political ambitions than any sort of legitimate inquiry.” Reitz, 39, previously worked as chief of staff for Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and became U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas over the summer after placing fourth in the Republican primary for Texas attorney general. Reitz also posted letters on X to Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass.; Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.; Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif.,; and Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif. He told NBC News this week that he was “not interested in chilling free speech.” Slotkin and five other sitting Democratic lawmakers were separately targeted by the Trump administration earlier this year over a video they posted to social media that sought to remind members of the military and intelligence communities that they should not obey unlawful orders. Allies of U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro tried to indict the six Democrats for their speech in that video, but federal grand jurors unanimously rejected the indictment attempt. Slotkin’s attorney, Prett Bharara, had previously written a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche cautioning him against following President Donald Trump’s public instruction to look into Slotkin’s political speech, which he dubbed a “criminal act.” Blanche has conceded that Slotkin’s words alone were “absolutely not a crime” and said at a press conference last week that there were “no ongoing investigations, criminal investigations, into words that incoming senators or congressmen have said.” Slotkin wrote in her letter that Reitz appeared to be “seeking attention” for himself and the Justice Department, or was “unaware” of basic constitutional rights. “Given all of this, your threats are frivolous and a violation of your ethical duties as an attorney,” she wrote. “I reserve all rights to take appropriate actions in the future as it relates to this sham investigation.”

images.caption: Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., at the U.S. Capitol on Feb. 4, 2026.
Aaron Reitz, U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, on Capitol Hill last year. Chip Somodevilla / Getty

Slotkin and five other sitting Democratic lawmakers were separately targeted by the Trump administration earlier this year over a video they posted to social media that sought to remind members of the military and intelligence communities that they should not obey unlawful orders. Allies of U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro tried to indict the six Democrats for their speech in that video, but federal grand jurors unanimously rejected the indictment attempt.

Slotkin's attorney, Prett Bharara, had previously written a letter to Attorney General Todd Blanche cautioning him against following President Donald Trump's public instruction to look into Slotkin's political speech, which he dubbed a "criminal act."

Blanche has conceded that Slotkin's words alone were "absolutely not a crime" and said at a press conference last week that there were "no ongoing investigations, criminal investigations, into words that incoming senators or congressmen have said."

Slotkin wrote in her letter that Reitz appeared to be "seeking attention" for himself and the Justice Department, or was "unaware" of basic constitutional rights.

"Given all of this, your threats are frivolous and a violation of your ethical duties as an attorney," she wrote. "I reserve all rights to take appropriate actions in the future as it relates to this sham investigation."

articles.title: Musk says he feels ‘foolish’ after GOP election spending spree
articles.summary: “I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money,” the tech billionaire said Wednesday.
articles.body:
Elon Musk, the world's richest man, expressed buyer's remorse Wednesday about his massive — and ultimately futile — spending spree to elect Republicans in the midterms.

The SpaceX and Tesla founder, who spent over $440 million backing GOP candidates, most of whom lost, acknowledged: "If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money." The comments came during The New York Times' DealBook Summit, where Musk also distanced himself from President Donald Trump's MAGA movement, maintaining "there are positives and negatives in both parties."

"I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much. Or maybe it would have been much worse without that," Musk said at the event, which he attended virtually from China, as he and other business leaders accompanied President Donald Trump to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. "But it certainly shows that American elections are not just about money."

Musk, who has experienced an on-again off-again relationship with Trump, was by far the biggest single donor this election cycle, spending at an unprecedented clip to support Republicans. But his efforts failed to make a major impact, as key GOP strongholds such as Texas, where he spent the bulk of his money, and Kansas flipped to Democrats.

Despite his midterm spending, Musk sought to clarify during Wednesday's public interview that he is "not MAGA" — regardless of his ties with the president. Instead, Musk claimed he supported a balance of power between Democrats and Republicans in the government.

"I'm not sure what MAGA means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that," Musk said.

These statements conflict with how Musk aligned with Trump in the past, even going as far to label himself as "Dark MAGA" when he campaigned for him just two years ago.

In fact, Musk appeared optimistic about working with the newly elected Democratic governor in Texas, where he runs massive SpaceX and Tesla operations. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, who has criticized the tech billionaire, has also said she is open to a "strong working relationship" with Musk.

"The new governor, actually, I think, is going to be quite moderate," Musk said. "I don't think she's sort of a far-left governor. And based on everything I've heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor."

articles.title: Elon Musk says he is ‘not MAGA’ after spending millions on Trump and his allies
articles.summary: Elon Musk struck a more moderate tone while discussing his political affiliation Wednesday, arguing that he does not have “blind adherence” to the policies of the Republican Party or MAGA.
articles.body: Elon Musk struck a more moderate tone while discussing his political affiliation Wednesday, arguing that he does not have “blind adherence” to the policies of the Republican Party or MAGA. The tech billionaire, who spent nearly $500 million in contributions to Republican campaigns and Trump allies ahead of the midterm elections, made the remarks while he was in China as part of President Donald Trump’s delegation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. “I’m not MAGA,” Musk said during an interview for the New York Times DealBook Summit. “If that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.” Musk, who moved his companies to Texas in 2020 after clashing with Democratic leaders in California, spent at least $168 million in Texas to uplift Trump allies in the midterm elections, including Senate candidate Ken Paxton and Gov. Greg Abbott, who both lost their bids. In the interview, Musk said that he thinks Democratic Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa will be “quite moderate” when she takes office. “I don’t think she’s sort of a far-left governor, and based on everything I’ve heard about her, I think things will be fine in Texas with Gina as governor,” Musk said. He argued that he spent big on campaigns because he thinks “it’s good to have some balance of power,” adding, “as a general rule” he wouldn’t want “the presidency, Senate and House all to be of the same party.” Musk said his goal, “which failed, by the way, obviously,” was to hold a Republican majority with 51 seats by 2029. “I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it,” Musk said. “But it certainly shows that, you know, American elections are not just about money.” He added, “Probably, if I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money.” “I think there are positives and negatives in both parties,” Musk said. “The truth is that, you know, both parties have their issues.” This is not the first time that Musk’s generous campaign donations have backfired. In 2025, he funneled at least $20 million into Wisconsin’s state Supreme Court race and offered $1 million checks to voters for backing the conservative candidate, who ultimately lost by 10 percentage points. After that campaign’s failures, Musk largely stayed out of the spotlight during the 2026 cycle. Some Republicans said privately that they wanted Musk to keep his distance, pointing to the success of his 2024 campaign strategy. Then, Musk spent over $250 million on Trump and the party, helping fuel Republicans’ victory in the race for the White House and control of Congress. The technique didn’t work in 2026, especially in Musk’s home state of Texas, where he has already been targeted by incoming officials. State Sen. Nathan Johnson, who will be the next state attorney general, pledged to investigate Musk over allegations that SpaceX unfairly benefited from a state grant program that was aimed at expanding and subsidizing rural broadband. Hinojosa and Democratic Sen.-elect James Talarico have also criticized Musk. While the governor-elect has made claims that Musk got tax breaks after donating to Abbott, Talarico has taken aim at the billionaire for wanting “his own personal United States senator.” Musk has also faced criticism from Democratic lawmakers who argue that he has too much influence over the White House. When Trump returned to office in 2025, Musk oversaw the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), the agency that prompted the firing of thousands of federal workers and the cancellation of various government funds. As of August 2026, more than 377,000 employees left the federal workforce due to job cuts directed by DOGE. The agency also led to the dismantling of the U.S. Agency for International Development and sweeping cuts to foreign aid.

articles.title: Trump says ‘we’ll wipe them out’ if Iran dirty bombs US
articles.summary: President Trump on Wednesday renewed his threat to annihilate Iran if it goes forward with its reported threat to launch a dirty bomb on U.S. soil. Fox News’s Jacqui Heinrich asked Trump while in Shenzen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit if Washington, D.C., residents should worry about Iran launching a dirty bomb…
articles.body:
President Trump on Wednesday renewed his threat to annihilate Iran if it goes forward with its reported threat to launch a dirty bomb on U.S. soil.

Fox News’s Jacqui Heinrich asked Trump while in Shenzen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit if Washington, D.C., residents should worry about Iran launching a dirty bomb on the city.

“I don’t think so, no,” he said. “I mean, look, if it does happen, we’ll wipe them out.”

The president said there was a “huge indication” that Iran has been “looking at gases, looking at bio,” referring to biological weapons, to attack the U.S. He said that using nuclear weapons “is much harder.”

“You know, these are nasty people,” Trump said. “We didn’t start this war. This was was started 51 years ago … you look at the USS Cole, where 400 of our kids were killed.”

The president previously said on Tuesday that he took the threat of the dirty bomb from Iran “very seriously” because “they happen to be crazy,” and he warned that the Islamic regime will “pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before.”

The alleged plot was reported by CNN and other outlets and suggested that U.S. intelligence indicates that Iran is developing plans to target senior administration officials by setting off a dirty bomb.

Some Trump administration officials have noted that threats from Iran have “substantially increased” and that the U.S. and its service members abroad “are under greater threat,” Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told lawmakers Wednesday.

Other officials have downplayed the CNN report. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Tuesday that “the homeland is secure,” and that there was no “new threat” from Iran’s “aspirational” planning.

Iranian officials have pushed back against the reporting. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei called the allegations “baseless” and a “fabricated media narrative” in a post on social platform X .

“RUBBISH. Spare us the Iraq War-style propaganda, especially with Israeli fingerprints all over it. Nobody is buying it,” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the reporting in an X post .

The U.S. is seen as particularly vulnerable to a dirty bomb attack. The weapon uses conventional explosives with radioactive material to contaminate the area and affect as many people in a dense urban area as possible. Washington is home to 700,000 people and brings in tens of thousands more who commute to work daily.

While a dirty bomb, also known as a “radiological dispersal device” (RDD), is considered far, far less damaging than a conventional nuclear bomb, the explosion of such a weapon could cause death or injury to anyone within the blast radius.

Democrat Matt Schultz suspended his campaign ahead…
articles.body:
Republican Rep. Nick Begich is projected to win a second term in Alaska’s at-large House district, according to Decision Desk HQ.

Begich beat out independent Bill Hill, who was backed by Democrats, as well as Democrat Eric Hafner and Libertarian James McDermott in the four-way general election showdown.

Democrat Matt Schultz suspended his campaign ahead of the primary, warning that “democracy itself is under threat” and calling on his supporters to back Hill.

After Begich and Hill advanced from this summer’s top-four, nonpartisan primary, Alaska’s Democratic Party also endorsed the independent over Hafner, who reportedly has no ties to the state and is incarcerated in New York .

Alaska is considered a solidly red state, but it’s also shown an openness to independents and moderate Democrats. Independent Bill Walker was elected governor in 2014, and Democrat Mary Peltola won the Last Frontier’s lone House seat in a 2022 special election before securing a full term.

The Republican clinched 51.35 percent of the vote over Hill’s 48.65, DDHQ projected Wednesday night just before 9:30 p.m. EST.

Begich won the seat for Republicans in 2024, ousting Peltola, who beat Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan for the Senate seat in this year’s midterms.

articles.title: Social Security raise: What’s left after the Medicare premium hike?
articles.summary: The math looks better for retirees in 2027 than it did this year.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Retirees are getting their biggest Social Security cost-of-living increase in four years, but higher Medicare Part B premiums will eat up some of that raise.

The standard Part B premium is rising $6.50 a month in 2027, which will trim the average Social Security bump from $75 to roughly $68.50 a month for retirees who have it deducted from their checks.

Put another way, the Part B premium hike will absorb about 9% of the $75 boost.

That’s good news for retirees after what happened this year , when a nearly $18 jump in the Part B premium ate into almost a third of the average Social Security raise.

But those figures are based on the average benefit. For retirees with smaller Social Security checks, the same Part B hike will take a bigger chunk out of their cost-of-living bump.

What the Part B hike means for your Social Security check

Social Security recipients are getting a 3.6% cost-of-living boost in January, which will raise the average benefit for retired workers by about $75 to $2,170 a month, according to the Social Security Administration .

The standard Part B premium will be $209.40 a month in 2027, so a retiree receiving the average benefit is left with roughly $1,960 after it’s deducted.

But many retirees get much smaller checks, and for those who have the premium withheld, the same $6.50 hike will consume a larger share of their raise.

Social Security increase before and after the Part B hike in 2027

Federal data shows more than 5.7 million retired workers received less than $1,000 a month in Social Security benefits in June.

For those getting $1,000 a month, the 3.6% COLA for 2027 will add $36, meaning the Part B increase will absorb about 18% of that raise.

If the premium goes up more than a retiree’s raise, the federal “ hold harmless ” rule can keep their Social Security check from shrinking, though that’s not expected to apply to many people next year.

Some Medicare Part B enrollees, around 9%, also pay a surcharge on top of the standard premium if their income is above a certain level. Those income thresholds for 2027 are listed here .

articles.title: Trump says people stockpiling food, water amid outages should ‘relax’
articles.summary: President Trump on Wednesday said that Americans purchasing and stockpiling canned food and water in response to the recent series of major outages should all “relax” and that “everything’s good.” Trump downplayed concerns over these outages in an interview with Fox News’s Jacqui Heinrich in Shenzen, China, saying that they were all “individual events. She…
articles.body:
President Trump on Wednesday said that Americans purchasing and stockpiling canned food and water in response to the recent series of major outages should all “relax” and that “everything’s good.”

Trump downplayed concerns over these outages in an interview with Fox News’s Jacqui Heinrich in Shenzen, China, saying that they were all “individual events. She later asked again about people stocking up on goods in the event of a larger outage.

“Tell them to relax, everything’s good,” he replied. “These are individual events.”

He added that if these incidents happened under former President Biden, “which was grossly incompetent and corrupt, nobody would have mentioned it.”

“These are not –– I’ll let you know if there’s a problem,” Trump said.

The president noted that these outages have happened after “putting in new equipment,” as outages with Apple and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) were both said to be connected to upgrades to their systems.

He emphasized the need for funding to refurbish the FAA’s digital infrastructure, and he said that all funding should not be spent “until we can do the whole thing, the whole system.”

“You don’t want to do piecemeal,” he said. “That’s what they did before –– I build, I build very well. I made a lot of money building things, always, and I know how to do this stuff, And I said, ‘Don’t.'”

He later said that the country will have the “best system anywhere in the world. Air traffic control, it’s called.”

Trump previously evaluated the outages when asked about them on Tuesday, telling reporters “ it’s fine .”

Fox News’s Laura Ingraham on Monday similarly asked Vice President Vance if Americans should stock up on food and water after countries in Europe made similar requests to their citizens.

“A lot of my friends have reached out asking if they should prepare to build a bunker or stock up on food and water,” Vance replied. “My answer to that is no. We don’t see a crisis coming down. But you have to be prepared for everything.”

Americans have seen a wave of outages affecting companies like Microsoft , Apple , and United Airlines , along with disruptions accessing J.P. Morgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo accounts. But facets of the federal government, specifically the FAA and the National Security Agency (NSA), have also been affected by downed systems.

The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop of all flights, the third in the last 25 years, last Thursday. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said it was likely due to a router being updated from copper-wiring to fiber optics at a radio post in Arkansas.

Trump told Heinrich that Duffy was “doing fantastic.”

Administration officials have also dismissed that any of these incidents were caused by cyberattacks or rogue AI. But Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin suggested that super intelligence (SI), the Trump administration’s preferred term for artificial intelligence, could have been behind the recent outages.

articles.title: Slotkin slams US attorney probing lawmakers as stunt for ‘publicity and your political ambitions’
articles.summary: Rep. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) on Wednesday fired back at the Texas-based U.S. attorney who penned letters threatening to investigate her and four other lawmakers, saying Aaron Reitz’s correspondence “is more about publicity and your political ambitions than any sort of legitimate inquiry.” Reitz wrote to Slotkin last week, posting the letter to X and writing…
articles.body:
Rep. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) on Wednesday fired back at the Texas-based U.S. attorney who penned letters threatening to investigate her and four other lawmakers, saying Aaron Reitz’s correspondence “is more about publicity and your political ambitions than any sort of legitimate inquiry.”

Reitz wrote to Slotkin last week, posting the letter to X and writing that comments she made about oversight investigations sending a deterrence message “sounds potentially illegal to me.”

Slotkin responded late Wednesday with a video and letter of her own, noting she has Speech and Debate Clause protections, calling his investigation “baseless” and saying he should “withdraw your letter immediately.”

“Your threats to prosecute a sitting senator for speech and legislative oversight also violate Justice Department policy. Your breach of these rules — publicly posting your letter instead of providing it directly to me, my attorney, or Senate Legal Counsel, is evidence that your threat of investigation is more about publicity and your political ambitions than any sort of legitimate inquiry,” she wrote.

“Exercising the power of a U.S. Attorney because you do not like my ‘political association, activities, or beliefs’ is also prohibited by the Justice Manual — and more importantly by the First Amendment and by the very criminal laws you mistakenly cited in your threat. As a United States Senator, I preserve my records as a matter of course. I have no intent of changing that practice now.”

Reitz’s letter cited comments from Slotkin noting that President Trump’s associates do not carry the immunity bestowed on the executive and saying investigating malfeasance of the administration could send a “deterrence message” to those interested in working in the Trump White House.

In her video message, Slotkin said she was being targeted “because I said aloud in a podcast that if you violate the law or waste taxpayer dollars, you should be held accountable.”

Alongside Slotkin , Reitz has sent letters to Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.). He also sent a letter to incoming House Oversight Chair Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), similarly demanding he preserve his records. In each, he has argued Democrats could be violating the law through their investigations.

Schiff, the latest recipient of a letter from Reitz, also responded Wednesday.

“No amount of bluster by this Justice Department will stop my efforts to expose the corruption and abuse of power at the heart of this administration,” he wrote on X.

“The American people demanded accountability and they will have it. I won’t back down. I won’t be intimidated. I have all the authority I need. It’s called Article I of the Constitution,” he added, citing the portion of the Constitution creating Congress.

In conducting widespread firings, the White House has repeatedly cited Trump’s Article II authority, the section that establishes the presidency.

Slotkin ended her letter by suggesting she may have an additional response to Reitz.

“I reserve all rights to take appropriate actions in the future as it relates to this sham investigation,” she wrote.

articles.title: Republican Nick Begich wins re-election to Alaska’s U.S. House seat, a rare bright spot for the GOP
articles.summary: JUNEAU, Alaska — Republican Rep. Nick Begich has won re-election to Alaska’s lone House seat, hanging on during a year that saw Democrats regain control in both houses of Congress.
articles.body: JUNEAU, Alaska — Republican Rep. Nick Begich has won re-election to Alaska’s lone House seat, hanging on during a year that saw Democrats regain control in both houses of Congress. His win Wednesday through the state’s ranked vote tabulation process was a rare bright spot for Republicans, whose ranks in the House were decimated in the midterms. It came a day after Democrat Mary Peltola flipped one of Alaska’s U.S. Senate seats by defeating two-term Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Begich was endorsed by President Donald Trump in seeking a second term and pitched himself as an effective leader who was in lockstep with the president’s efforts to expand oil and gas drilling and other resource development in the state. In a statement after his win, Begich said he takes the job of U.S. representative seriously and thanked the other candidates. “This process requires engagement, and the perspectives brought forward during the campaign added value for Alaskans as they made important decisions about their vote in this race,” he said. His main challenger was independent Bill Hill, a commercial fisherman and retired teacher who was endorsed by the state Democratic Party. He sought to focus on affordability issues, limiting the influence of big money in elections and pushing back against the billionaire class in the U.S. Hill said he called Begich to congratulate him. “I wished him well as he continues representing Alaska in Congress, because all Alaskans have a stake in his success,” Hill said in a statement. The race was one of the last House races to be called nationally. Once the ranked choice tabulations were complete, Begich finished with nearly 51.4% of the vote, while Hill had nearly 48.7%. The contest also included Democrat Eric Hafner, who is incarcerated in a federal prison in New York after being convicted in 2022 of threatening to kill judges, police officers and others. Hill’s campaign had expressed concerns over Hafner’s candidacy, particularly in the final weeks of the race, distributing stickers and yard signs labeling him a “fake ‘Democrat.’” Hafner, who received nearly 8% of the vote after the Nov. 3 general election, submitted a candidate biography that appeared in state election materials that made no reference to his incarceration. Hill’s campaign and state Democrats had cried foul after voters were sent text messages from an undisclosed source supporting Hafner. Hill’s campaign manager, Kevin Groh, and the Democratic Party’s executive director, Jenny-Marie Stryker, said they never learned who sponsored the texts. Stryker said the party spent “thousands of dollars to send texts clarifying that the real Alaska Democratic Party endorsed Bill Hill.” Hafner’s mother, Carol “Kitty” Hafner, responded this week to an email from The Associated Press that was sent to her son. She said it would seem “next to impossible” for voters not to know he was in prison, given the coverage of his candidacy for Alaska’s House seat in 2024. She also said the “media has gone well overboard identifying his incarceration status.” “Absolutely no one encouraged” Hafner to run, his mother wrote, adding that his campaigns have been “entirely independent of any influencers.” “Tell President Trump to Pardon Eric Hafner!” she wrote. Both she and her son lack ties to the state. Carol Hafner ran in Alaska’s Senate primary in August, finishing sixth with 0.6% of the vote. They have run for office in Alaska and other states before. The major candidates in the U.S. Senate race were Peltola and Sullivan. But the race also included a second Sullivan — Dan J. Sullivan. Peltola faced allegations that members of her team helped recruit the second Sullivan, but she denied involvement in any such effort. “I personally know that I am innocent, so I don’t spend a lot of time hand-wringing” about it, she said in an interview Wednesday after her win. The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation, but Alaska’s U.S. attorney has not said what potential crimes authorities were looking into.
